chunks: And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

“Whoever says in his Witr, when he performs Witr: ‘I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, and I repent to Him,’ seventy times, and persists in that until a year passes, Allah will record him with Himself among ‘those who seek forgiveness at daybreak,’ and Paradise and forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, become obligatory for him.”

key_terms.أَتُوبُ: I repent; I return to Allah in repentance
key_terms.أَسْتَغْفِرُ: I seek forgiveness; a formula of repentance and plea for pardon
key_terms.وَتْرِهِ: his Witr prayer, the single-unit concluding prayer of the night prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying istighfar seventy times in the Witr prayer for a year?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages persistent seeking of forgiveness in the Witr prayer by repeating a formula of istighfar seventy times. It links this devotional practice to being counted among those who seek forgiveness before dawn and promises divine forgiveness and jannah for one who maintains it for a full year.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1405 - It is narrated from Umar ibn Yazid that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"Whoever says during his Witr prayer (while performing the single-unit prayer of Witr) 'Astaghfirullah Rabbi wa Atubu Ilayh' (I seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), and I turn to Him in repentance) seventy times, and continues to do so regularly until a year passes, Allah (swt) will write him among 'those who seek forgiveness in the early hours of the morning,' and Paradise and forgiveness from Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, will become obligatory for him."
